newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian 1997 budget to target health, education.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian 1997 budget to target health, education.

text.p: Ivory Coast's government has published outlines of a 1997 budget draft which envisages a 1.1 percent increase in total spending to 1,786.1 billion CFA francs and a shift towards more spending on health and education.

The outlines, published on Thursday as part of a cabinet statement, do not make clear precisely how spending will be redistributed but diplomatic sources said that the final draft would include a freeze on current spending by ministries.

"Basically they are freezing current expenditure of ministries, which is itself useful," one source said, adding that the draft to be presented to parliament had a legal significance but had no use as an economic management tool.

The government statement, published after Wednesday's cabinet meeting, said economic discipline and budgetary rigour were the guiding principles. It listed increased education and professional training and health services among its targets.

It predicted targets of seven percent for Gross Domestic Product growth and three percent for inflation. Inflation in 1996 appears on course for the government target of five percent with GDP growth projected at around seven percent.
The 1997 draft includes projected tax and other internal revenue, such as privatisation, totalling 1,240.6 billion CFA francs, including a seven percent increase on 1996 tax receipts.

It includes a further 545.5 billion in external resources -- international budgetary assistance, gifts and foreign project-based loans and a projected 192.5 billion CFA franc saving on debt servicing due to Paris Club rescheduling.
